# Prototype component BOM

Status: Stage 3 conditional selection, 2026-10-08. Every MPN below is UNVERIFIED for final hardware release. This is a reviewable prototype inventory, not procurement authorization, a manufactured board or a qualification certificate. Native library checks and supplied manufacturer research are identified separately. The original targets remain 4.75-5.25 V, 500 mA TOTAL external continuous load, strictly <2 mA unloaded VBUS, and component cost <USD 8 at Q100.

## Fitted components

| Refdes | Value | Footprint | MPN | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| J1 | USB4105-GF-A | Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_GCT_USB4105-xx-A_16P_TopMnt_Horizontal | USB4105-GF-A | UNVERIFIED: GCT 16-contact USB-C power input; supplied manufacturer rating 5 A combined VBUS contacts, 48 V DC [G1,G2]. Use Connector:USB_C_Receptacle_USB2.0_16P. Model-specific footprint resolves; exact drawing overlay, board-edge fit and exposed fine-pitch hand-solder access remain release checks. Insulation leakage belongs to the board/connector bin. |
| U1 | TPS2065CDBVR | Package_TO_SOT_SMD:SOT-23-5 | TPS2065CDBVR | UNVERIFIED: TI 1 A continuous active high-side switch, 4.5-5.5 V, fixed 1.2-1.9 A IOS, active-high EN [T1,T2]. Use Power_Management:TPS2065CDBV. Five accessible perimeter leads, no exposed underside pad. Removes external programming-current ambiguity; 90 uA ISE is specified at IOUT=0 and does not by itself close LED-loaded idle current or fault qualification. |
| J2 | 1984617 | TerminalBlock_Phoenix:TerminalBlock_Phoenix_PT-1,5-2-3.5-H_1x02_P3.50mm_Horizontal | 1984617 | UNVERIFIED: Phoenix PT 1,5/2-3,5-H, 2-pin 3.50 mm screw terminal, 17.5 A nominal, 1.20 mm recommended holes [P1]. Use Connector:Screw_Terminal_01x02. Supplied dimensions match the selected footprint family; support housing during tightening and verify actual fabrication/assembly. No active IQ; insulation leakage remains allocated. |
| J3 | M20-9980246 | Connector_PinHeader_2.54mm:PinHeader_2x02_P2.54mm_Vertical | M20-9980246 | UNVERIFIED: Harwin four-contact 2x2 2.54 mm vertical THT header, 3 A/contact [H1-H3]. Use Connector_Generic:Conn_02x02_Odd_Even. Require finished holes 0.97-1.07 mm; footprint nominal drill 1.00 mm is conditional on that tolerance. Unkeyed mating and scarce stock remain risks. No active IQ; count insulation leakage. |
| R1 | 5.1k | Resistor_SMD:R_0603_1608Metric | RC0603FR-075K1L | UNVERIFIED: YAGEO 5.1 kohm +/-1%, +/-100 ppm/C, 0.1 W 0603 [R1S,R3S]; Device:R. Dedicated CC1-to-GND Rd; do not join CC2. Current comes from the source CC pin, not VBUS. Verify source-specific CC dissipation and assembled value. |
| R2 | 5.1k | Resistor_SMD:R_0603_1608Metric | RC0603FR-075K1L | UNVERIFIED: same exact resistor and ratings [R1S,R3S]; Device:R. Independent CC2-to-GND Rd supports the other orientation. Its source-CC current is separate from VBUS; verify separation and value physically. |
| R4 | 10k | Resistor_SMD:R_0603_1608Metric | RC0603FR-0710KL | UNVERIFIED: YAGEO 10 kohm +/-1%, +/-100 ppm/C, 0.1 W 0603 [R2S,R3S]; Device:R. Limits D1 current; conservative 0-50 C model gives <0.532 mA and <2.80 mW at 5.25 V, allocated 0.540 mA. Aging/assembly variation and visibility remain qualification checks. |
| C1 | 1uF | Capacitor_SMD:C_0603_1608Metric | CC0603KRX7R9BB105 | UNVERIFIED: YAGEO 1 uF +/-10%, 50 V X7R 0603 [C1S,C2S]; Device:C. Place adjacent to U1 IN/GND. Nominal value exceeds TI minimum 0.1 uF bypass, but guaranteed effective capacitance with DC bias/aging and leakage over the prototype range remain unclosed. |
| C2 | 1uF | Capacitor_SMD:C_0603_1608Metric | CC0603KRX7R9BB105 | UNVERIFIED: same exact 1 uF capacitor [C1S,C2S]; Device:C. Protected-rail local bypass. Include leakage in VBUS total and switched-load demand; qualify startup, load capacitance, transients and effective capacitance. |
| D1 | WP710A10LID | LED_THT:LED_D3.0mm | WP710A10LID | UNVERIFIED: Kingbright low-current red 3 mm THT LED [L1,L2]; Device:LED. Supplied 2.54 mm lead pitch and 0.9 mm recommended holes match footprint. Brightness/Vf are specified at 2 mA, so visibility near 0.3 mA is unproven. Follow documented lead-heating limits and qualify prototype hand assembly. |

R3 is intentionally absent, not a missing BOM row: the selected switch has a fixed current limit and no ILIM pin. ILIM_SET is retired. No FLT pull-up or EN resistor is fitted because FLT is unobserved and active-high EN connects directly to VBUS_RAW. No MCU, converter, firmware, RF, TVS or other auxiliary VBUS load is fitted. The latter absence makes no ESD/transient immunity claim. Rationale: avoid obsolete programming hardware and unnecessary standing-current paths.

## Capture contract and native evidence

On 2026-10-08 this run actually found the U1/J1/J2/J3/LED symbols with search_symbols, obtained all seven real symbol pin maps with symbol_pins, and resolved all seven unique footprint IDs above as OK. Bare R and C search queries returned no matches; exact Device:R and Device:C pin lookups succeeded with two passive pins each. This is positive installed-library evidence, not a reason to invent substitutes. No schematic exists as a result of these lookups.

- U1 Power_Management:TPS2065CDBV: 1 OUT power_out to +5V_PROTECTED; 2 GND power_in to GND; 3 ~FLT open_collector intentional no-connect; 4 EN input to VBUS_RAW; 5 IN power_in to VBUS_RAW. Supplied TI DBV pinout agrees. Do not use MIC2544's ground-enabled or dual-OUT pin map.
- J1 Connector:USB_C_Receptacle_USB2.0_16P: A4/A9/B4/B9 to VBUS_RAW; A1/A12/B1/B12 and S1 shield to GND; A5 to CC1; B5 to CC2. A6/A7/A8/B6/B7/B8 are individually intentional no-connects for D+/D-/SBU; there is no USB data function. Direct shield-to-GND is an explicit prototype choice with no extra resistor/capacitor; EMC/ESD performance is unqualified.
- J2 Connector:Screw_Terminal_01x02: 1 to +5V_PROTECTED, 2 to GND. Supplied unrotated footprint centers: 1=(0,0), 2=(3.5,0) mm. Viewed from component side in the footprint's +X direction, pad 2 is right of pad 1; actual layout rotation still needs labels.
- J3 Connector_Generic:Conn_02x02_Odd_Even: 1/3 to +5V_PROTECTED; 2/4 to GND. Unrotated centers: 1=(0,0), 2=(2.54,0), 3=(0,2.54), 4=(2.54,2.54) mm. Do not rely on equal current sharing or an unkeyed plug's orientation.
- R1 Device:R: 1 to CC1, 2 to GND. R2: 1 to CC2, 2 to GND. R4: 1 to +5V_PROTECTED, 2 to LED_A. R pins are passive and interchangeable physically; use these assignments consistently.
- C1 Device:C: 1 to VBUS_RAW, 2 to GND. C2: 1 to +5V_PROTECTED, 2 to GND. These are nonpolar ceramics with passive pins.
- D1 Device:LED: 1 K to GND, 2 A to LED_A. Footprint pad 1 is rectangular at (0,0), pad 2 at (2.54,0), 0.9 mm drills. Confirm the actual package cathode before soldering.

## Electrical review and complete conditional current ledger

Conditions: 4.75-5.25 V, assumed dry indoor 0-50 C ambient, outputs externally open, U1 enabled and settled, no backfeed/fault. Device TJ must remain within its documented range. The operating target is strictly <2 mA VBUS, not <=2 mA. Source-CC current in R1/R2 is a separate source interface; the support research's illustrative 0.700 mA CC allowance is neither a universal bound nor added to this VBUS-only metric.

- D1/R4: allocate 0.540 mA. With Vf>=0, 10 kohm, +/-1% and 100 ppm/C over a 25 C departure from reference, Rmin=9875.25 ohm and I<=0.531633 mA. This excludes unquantified aging/process shifts; resistor dissipation is <2.80 mW versus 100 mW at 70 C. Approximate intended LED current is (5-1.7)/10k=0.33 mA, but 1.7 V is characterized at 2 mA and cannot guarantee that current or visibility.
- U1 IN internal bias: allocate 0.190 mA. Of this, 0.090 mA is the supplied datasheet maximum ISE at IOUT=0, VIN 4.5-5.5 V, EN=VIN, TJ -40 to +125 C; the additional 0.100 mA is an ASSUMED reserve for the different LED-loaded operating condition, not device evidence. Actual bias at this operating condition remains unbounded by the supplied extract.
- U1 EN terminal: separately reserve positive leakage 0.001 mA from the supplied +/-1 uA limit. EN is a separate terminal; if later measurement/evidence includes it in a whole-device figure, charge it only once. No external RSET exists.
- External FLT pull-up and EN bias resistor: 0 mA because absent. FLT is open, so its 1 uA off-leakage under externally imposed voltage does not create an external VBUS-fed load. Internal device behavior remains in the bias bin.
- C1/C2: combined 0.050 mA ASSUMED leakage acceptance bin. Each selected capacitor has supplied 100 Mohm IR under rated-voltage/15-35 C test conditions, equivalent to 0.5 uA at 50 V. Do not extrapolate this as a guarantee at 0/50 C. Keep both capacitors in the total, with C2 also a switched-rail load.
- J1/J2/J3, PCB insulation and any residual non-device leakage: 0.050 mA ASSUMED bin. They have no active quiescent supply, but real contamination/insulation leakage is not zero and has not been bounded. No additional protection-device leakage is present in this inventory.
- Other VBUS loads: 0 by the ten-refdes inventory. R1/R2 CC currents are not powered from VBUS on this board.

Conditional allocation sum = 0.540+0.190+0.001+0+0.050+0.050+0 = 0.831 mA; headroom to the exclusive boundary = 1.169 mA. This preserves margin for a plausible prototype, but actual whole-board worst-case compliance is UNKNOWN until the bias and leakage assumptions are justified. Do not describe 0.831 mA as a measured current or manufacturer-guaranteed maximum. A failed bin requires a documented correction/redesign; no electrical target may be relaxed.

For the normal load, conservatively assign all 0.100 mA leakage reserves downstream: switched demand <=500+0.540+0.100=500.640 mA, conditional on those bins. TI's 1 A continuous rating and IOS minimum 1.2 A exceed that load; IOS maximum 1.9 A is a fault-design case, not a 500 mA cap. The TPS2051C 0.5 A continuous variant is not substituted. Supplied DBV RDS(on) max 154 milliohm gives 77.10 mV switch drop and 38.60 mW conduction loss at 0.500640 A. At 4.75 V, switch-only output is about 4.67290 V under those conditions; connector and copper losses further reduce it and remain to be budgeted. Harwin's 20 milliohm/contact figure, if applicable to the chosen mating path, gives 20 mV for a two-contact 500 mA loop; other contacts/copper are not thereby bounded. There is no new regulated output-voltage guarantee.

Fault model established by supplied TI evidence: active current limiting with static IOS 1.2-1.9 A, and disabled-output discharge for the chosen non--2 variant. EN remains high in normal operation. Dynamic overshoot is not bounded by 1.9 A; the instantaneous 5.25 V x 1.9 A short-circuit dissipation scale is about 9.98 W before accounting for dynamic/thermal behavior, vastly above normal I-squared-R loss. Exact thermal/recovery details were not extracted in the supplied follow-up and must be reviewed from T1 before fault testing/release. Do not reuse MIC2544's foldback/cycling narrative or invent thresholds. Both outputs and LED share the affected rail; no channel isolation or safe indefinite short claim is made. Validate fault removal recovery with an energy-limited known-capable source/cable. Outputs are loads only; no reverse-current blocking, external output powering or paralleling supplies is permitted.

C1/C2 nominal 1 uF exceeds the supplied TI >=0.1 uF input-bypass recommendation, but capacitance tolerance, +/-15% X7R temperature change, DC bias and aging must be considered together. No guaranteed effective minimum is available in the supplied extract. Validate source startup, external load capacitance, overshoot and short/recovery behavior.

## Mechanical correspondence and manual-assembly conditions

- U1: TI DBV0005A drawing has five perimeter terminals and no underside exposed pad, consistent with installed SOT-23-5. Native pin map agrees with TI. Check actual recommended-land overlay and solder access at board review; a standard package identifier is not a manufacturing certificate.
- J1: exact GCT-model footprint and native contact map chosen; supplied GCT drawings/rating support this identity. A complete footprint/drawing overlay and board-edge placement are still pending. Retain exposed fine-pitch solder-row risk and shell-anchor/plug-access checks.
- J2: supplied Phoenix body 7.00 x 7.55 mm, 3.50 mm pin pitch, 1.20 mm recommended drill. Installed footprint body 7.00 x 7.60 mm, pad centers 3.50 mm, 1.20 mm drills and 2.40 mm pads. The 0.05 mm body-depth difference is disclosed; review fabrication annulus and finished holes. Support housing during 0.22-0.25 N m tightening, not through solder joints alone; specified wire range 0.2-1.5 mm2, strip 5 mm.
- J3: supplied body 5.08 x 5.08 mm and 2.54 mm grid agree with footprint. Finished holes must be 0.97-1.07 mm; a 1.00 mm nominal drill with ordinary +/-0.10 mm process is not sufficient. Confirm fabricated plated-hole specification and lead insertion sample. Unkeyed mating, 8.64 mm height and mating/strain relief require review.
- R1/R2/R4 and C1/C2: supplied 0603 body/terminal geometry overlaps the standard installed 0603 lands; all are >=0603. This is prototype geometric compatibility, not validated solder yield.
- D1: supplied 2.54 mm pitch/0.9 mm recommended holes match installed LED_D3.0mm. Respect lead-heating limits: 260 C for 3 s at 2 mm below base or 5 s at 5 mm per L1; do not heat epoxy or stress hot leads. L2 recommends manual soldering only for repair/rework, so initial prototype hand assembly remains an explicit process qualification, not manufacturer-certified production.

The target remains <=40 x 30 mm, two layers, 1 oz, nominal 1.6 mm FR-4; assumed no holes/enclosure. Accessible leaded parts support a conditional hand-assembled prototype. Phoenix describes wave assembly and Harwin gives solder-heat tests rather than a verified iron recipe; qualify actual technique. No layout exists here, so board fit, all courtyards, screwdriver/wire/plug access, copper fault capability and thermal area remain genuine downstream obligations.

## Complete per-board Q100 cost estimate

All figures are USD/component, supplied public observations dated 2026-10-08, excluding PCB, assembly, shipping, taxes and unverified destination/cart charges. These are not purchases or guaranteed quotes.

- J1 USB4105-GF-A: 0.57450 at Q100 [G3], original supplied snapshot.
- U1 TPS2065CDBVR: 0.51640 at Q100 cut tape [T3], 20:41 UTC; page showed 9,748 stock, not checkout-verified. Optional reel fee excluded because cut tape selected for estimating.
- J2 1984617: 0.59000 ESTIMATE ONLY for a Q100 board. [P2] exposed only Q1=0.59000; no Q100 tier was verified. Do not call this a Q100 quotation.
- J3 M20-9980246: 0.13410 at Q100 [H4], 20:47 UTC. Page showed only 5 stock and 22-week standard lead time; Q100 immediate procurement is not established.
- R1 RC0603FR-075K1L: 0.01100 at 100+ [R4S].
- R2 RC0603FR-075K1L: 0.01100 at 100+ [R4S]. At 100 boards two per board means 200 units; use the quoted 100+ tier conservatively, without inventing a further discount.
- R4 RC0603FR-0710KL: 0.01100 at 100+ [R5S].
- C1 CC0603KRX7R9BB105: 0.28370 at Q100 [C3S].
- C2 CC0603KRX7R9BB105: 0.28370 at Q100 [C3S]; 200 total for 100 boards, no invented quantity discount.
- D1 WP710A10LID: 0.12850 at Q100 [L3].

Subtotal excluding J2 = 1.95390; including the explicitly uncertain J2 estimate = 2.54390 per board, or 254.39 for 100 boards. Estimated headroom below USD 8 = 5.45610 per board. A Q100 component total is therefore plausibly below target on the disclosed estimate, but formal quote/availability compliance is unverified. J2 could cost up to strictly less than 6.04610 per board only if all other figures remained valid; this arithmetic is not permission to spend or a supplier quote.

## Selection decision and remaining release checks

The prior Stage 2 all-evidence-before-BOM freeze criterion is explicitly revised in SPEC, SUBSYSTEMS and the constraint registry: select UNVERIFIED parts for the requested reviewable prototype, while preserving all electrical targets and mandatory qualification before release. No software gate is waived and a known violating candidate must still be replaced. This sequencing decision is recorded; it does not certify an all-temperature worst case.

Still pending: exact J1/U1 land/drawing overlay; PCB fit/courtyards and hole tolerances; source/cable entitlement and startup; effective capacitor minimum; LED visibility; non-overlapping bias/leakage closure over 4.75-5.25 V and 0-50 C; 500 mA on either output and shared; all loaded contact/copper drops; exact TI thermal/recovery review; current-limit spread/dynamic overshoot; sustained-short thermal behavior and fault recovery; hand-assembly trial; final Q100 quote and header availability. No physical test has run. Preserve the original downstream schematic, ERC, symbol verification, legibility, PCB/DRC, exports and firmware-stage applicability/blocker reports. The fitted BOM has no programmable part, so onboard firmware remains not applicable; confirm against the actual schematic later.

## Source ledger

Manufacturer facts and prices below were independently researched and supplied to this stage on 2026-10-08; this stage did not itself browse. Native search/pin/footprint results above are actual current-run tool output. Source-conditioned calculations are engineering review, not measurements.

# Protected USB-C 500 mA Power Breakout Specification

Status: requirements seed for an independent, reviewable prototype. No prototype has been manufactured or physically tested. Candidate parts and estimates below are not approved selections or verified hardware results.

## Provenance and interpretation

REQUIRED identifies the original product brief. ASSUMED identifies a proposed default or preliminary allocation not supplied as a requirement. SUPPLIED RESEARCH identifies additional public research embedded in the 2026-10-08 brief; this stage has not independently browsed those sources, verified prices, or run local library/pin/footprint checks. Proposed design choices require later confirmation. Every decision includes its rationale. Requirements and assumptions are recorded alongside their machine-readable constraint records.

The prior searches returned no existing design-document content. The validated proposal established an OpenSpec workspace, so this change seeds per-capability scenarios as well as this specification. No KiCad source is modified in this requirements stage.

## Budgets

The following is the complete preliminary unloaded-current accounting framework, not a claim of verified compliance. All entries below are VBUS input-current allocations in mA. Supplied component research has not been independently inspected in this stage. The actual total remains UNKNOWN until conditions and leakage bounds are established. Do not accept the candidate merely because its nominal LED and IC currents appear small.

Source conditions: attached nominal-5 V USB-C source, input within 4.75-5.25 V, both external output connectors unloaded, switch enabled and settled, LED illuminated, no fault and no other power source/backfeed. Check both range endpoints and any internal maxima across temperature/tolerances. CC Rd current is supplied on CC by the source and is accounted separately from this board's VBUS-input current; it is not silently omitted from the USB attachment design.

| Accounting bin | Preliminary ceiling (mA) | Evidence status |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Protected-rail LED and 10 kohm 1% resistor | 0.531 | Conservative resistor calculation; selected LED and visibility unverified |
| Enabled switch internal supply/control | 0.160 | Supplied research; conditions and current-definition boundary unverified |
| Additional ILIM/control current excluded from supply-current figure | 1.000 | ASSUMED allocation; actual upper bound unknown |
| External pull-ups/bias | 0 | ASSUMED intentionally absent; topology confirmation pending |
| Input/output capacitor leakage | 0.050 | ASSUMED allocation; bounds unknown |
| PCB/connector/other fitted protection leakage | 0.050 | ASSUMED allocation; inventory and bounds unknown |
| Other VBUS-fed loads | 0 | ASSUMED none; revisit after component selection |
| Allocation sum | 1.791 | Conditional planning total only |
| Unallocated distance to exclusive 2 mA boundary | 0.209 | Headroom, not a fitted load or measured margin |

Resolve the supply-current definition before summing real device currents: if ILIM or EN current is already included in the IC figure, charge it once to that bin; otherwise derive and include its separate worst-case contribution. If the candidate cannot meet the whole-board requirement after legitimate reallocation, reject the candidate rather than relaxing the brief.

- **power.input_voltage_v**: REQUIRED: nominal 5 V USB-C VBUS input; guaranteed design operating range must cover 4.75 to 5.25 V. No guaranteed operation or sustained-short performance at 6 V is required.
  - Rationale: The operating range is distinct from a component absolute-maximum stress rating.
- **power.external_continuous_load_ma**: REQUIRED: deliver up to and including 500 mA TOTAL normal continuous external load across the two parallel outputs; either connector must carry the full 500 mA when used alone. The LED and protection/control currents are additional input demand, not part of that external-load allowance.
  - Rationale: Parallel connectors share one load budget and one protection block.
- **power.unloaded_vbus_current_ma**: REQUIRED: total steady-state unloaded VBUS input current is strictly LESS THAN 2 mA, with both external outputs open and the protection enabled. The numeric boundary 2 is exclusive. Count LED, enabled protection/control, programming and pull-up currents not already included in another entry, all leakage, and every other fitted VBUS-fed load. Demonstrate the worst case throughout 4.75-5.25 V and the ASSUMED ambient range, including component tolerances. Startup and fault current are separate operating cases, not disguised as unloaded steady-state current.
  - Rationale: An incomplete or nominal-only sum cannot establish compliance.
- **budget.led_current_ma**: ASSUMED design candidate/allocation: a protected-rail LED with a 10 kohm, 1% series resistor has a conservative current ceiling of 0.531 mA at 5.25 V, using Rmin = 9900 ohm and the deliberately conservative bound Vf >= 0 V: 5.25/9900 = 0.530304 mA, rounded upward. No minimum brightness or actual LED Vf has yet been verified.
  - Rationale: This ceiling avoids inventing an LED forward-voltage specification; visibility still needs checking.
- **budget.enabled_switch_current_ma**: ASSUMED preliminary allocation: 0.160 mA for enabled switch supply/control current. SUPPLIED RESEARCH reports a 160 microampere maximum for MIC2544-2YM under datasheet conditions; the exact conditions, full operating-range coverage, and inclusion or exclusion of ILIM and other terminal currents remain unverified.
  - Rationale: The reported value is a starting evidence lead, not an independently confirmed whole-board bound.
- **budget.programming_control_extra_ma**: ASSUMED preliminary allocation: at most 1.000 mA of additional VBUS input current for ILIM programming and control paths EXCLUDED from the preceding supply-current definition. The actual upper bound is UNKNOWN. If the datasheet includes a contribution in supply current, count it there only and do not also count it here.
  - Rationale: An explicit unresolved allocation exposes the programming-current risk without double counting or claiming it is satisfied.
- **budget.external_pullup_current_ma**: ASSUMED preliminary allocation: 0 mA for external pull-ups because the proposed always-enabled, unmonitored implementation fits no FLG pull-up and no VBUS-fed EN bias resistor. This zero applies only if that topology is confirmed electrically suitable for the exact variant. Any later fitted bias or pull-up must receive its own worst-case current entry.
  - Rationale: An unused open-drain status signal does not need a pull-up merely to create a logic level nobody reads.
- **budget.capacitor_leakage_ma**: ASSUMED preliminary allocation: input and output capacitor leakage combined must be at most 0.050 mA at worst-case voltage and temperature. Actual component leakage bounds have not been obtained.
  - Rationale: Decoupling leakage belongs in the unloaded input-current total.
- **budget.board_connector_protection_leakage_ma**: ASSUMED preliminary allocation: at most 0.050 mA combined for connector/PCB insulation leakage and any other fitted VBUS-connected protection-device leakage not already included above. Actual bounds and any added-device list remain unverified.
  - Rationale: Leakage paths and future protection additions must not disappear from the current accounting.
- **budget.other_vbus_loads_ma**: ASSUMED preliminary allocation: 0 mA for other VBUS-fed loads because none are currently proposed. This is an inventory assumption, not a measured zero. Adding any load requires updating the budget and its constraint record.
  - Rationale: The design has no processor, firmware, converter, or other planned auxiliary consumer.
- **budget.unloaded_planning_total_ma**: ASSUMED allocation sum: 0.531 + 0.160 + 1.000 + 0 + 0.050 + 0.050 + 0 = 1.791 mA, leaving 0.209 mA below the exclusive 2 mA boundary. This is a planning allocation, NOT a verified worst-case device-current sum. The actual worst-case total is UNKNOWN until every contribution has a justified bound and non-overlapping accounting. Reallocations require documentation and must preserve the strictly below 2 mA requirement.

## Provenance and explicit sequencing revision

REQUIRED retains the original product brief. ASSUMED denotes engineering defaults, budgets and conditions. SUPPLIED RESEARCH denotes the independently researched manufacturer/distributor evidence supplied to this stage, not browsing by this stage. LOCAL-TOOL EVIDENCE denotes actual current-run symbol search, pin and footprint output. No source-conditioned calculation or software check is a physical measurement.

The selected fixed-limit switch eliminates the external RSET network. # Subsystem architecture: protected USB-C 500 mA breakout

Status: Stage 2 architecture draft, 2026-10-08. Source of requirements: docs/SPEC.md and the five OpenSpec capability specs. The proposal define-independent-500ma-architecture has passed validation. No schematic or PCB is changed here; no prototype has been built or physically tested. This document defines the topology and selection gates, not an approved component BOM or proof of electrical compliance.

## 1. Prose block diagram and interface contract

A known-capable nominal-5 V USB-C source and cable feed J1. Its VBUS contacts join VBUS_RAW; its ground contacts join GND. C1 decouples VBUS_RAW close to the common high-side active protection U1. U1 supplies +5V_PROTECTED. Only that protected rail feeds C2, both parallel external output connectors J2/J3, and the series R4/D1 power indicator. GND is the shared return. No connector or indicator branch bypasses U1.

Separately, J1 CC1 connects through R1 to GND, and CC2 through R2 to GND. CC1 and CC2 remain distinct. In the candidate MIC2544 implementation, R3 sets the protection threshold via ILIM_SET; the reported active-low enable is tied to GND, and unused FLG and NC remain unconnected after exact-device confirmation. The LED branch is +5V_PROTECTED -> R4 -> LED_A -> D1 anode, with D1 cathode at GND. This is functional intent; unverified connector/passive symbol pin numbers are not wiring authority.

Rationale: one active protection domain covers both outputs and the indicator, while separate CC terminations support attachment in either plug orientation.

ASSUMED architecture identifiers: J1 USB-C input; U1 common high-side protection; J2 2-pin screw terminal; J3 2x2 header; R1/R2 separate CC1/CC2 Rd; R3 ILIM setting resistor; R4 LED resistor; D1 indicator; C1 input and C2 output decoupling. Proposed nets are VBUS_RAW, +5V_PROTECTED, GND, CC1, CC2, ILIM_SET, and LED_A. These are a documentation contract, not evidence of existing schematic instances. Later artifacts must use these exact identifiers or revise the architecture and related records together.

Rationale: stable identifiers prevent the architecture, eventual BOM, pinout, and schematic from describing different circuits.

## 2. USB-C input and attachment subsystem

- Required input: 4.75-5.25 V at the board; no guarantee at 6 V. A 7 V absolute-maximum IC rating cannot establish an operating guarantee.
- R1 and R2: separate 5.1 kohm Rd, assumed 1% and accessible packages at least 0603. Never join CC1 and CC2. Verify their actual symbol pins and connector pad assignments before capture.
- J1 candidate: GCT USB4105-GF-A. Connect all relevant VBUS and GND contacts according to its verified drawing and library mapping, not by assuming one symbol pin represents one physical contact.
- No USB data function, PD negotiation, advertised-current sensing, or voltage conversion. Data/SBU contacts have no functional connection; deliberate no-connect markings and the shell/ground treatment must be resolved from the selected connector and documented during part selection/capture. Do not invent a shell-to-ground component here.
- Full-load use is restricted to a known-capable source/cable supporting 500 mA external load plus board overhead and startup demand. Rd establishes attachment; it neither negotiates a power contract nor limits the board to advertised current. CC-source current is separate from the VBUS-input budget.

LOCAL-TOOL EVIDENCE on 2026-10-08: check_footprints resolves Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_GCT_USB4105-xx-A_16P_TopMnt_Horizontal. No USB connector symbol pins, pad geometry, manufacturer drawing correspondence, or assembly suitability were verified in this architecture stage. USB4105-GF-A remains a candidate; the supplied 5 A combined VBUS-contact rating and 48 V DC rating remain supplied research.

Rationale: connector availability, contact ratings, mechanical correspondence, and USB source entitlement are separate checks. No generic USB-source compliance is claimed for a passive-Rd-only breakout.

## 3. Active protection and power distribution subsystem

### Candidate device and local evidence

CANDIDATE, not an accepted part: MIC2544-2YM. Stage 2 local-tool evidence on 2026-10-08 confirms installed symbol Power_Management:MIC2544-2YM, one unit with pins 1 ~{EN} input, 2 FLG open_collector, 3 GND power_in, 4 ILIM input, 5 NC no_connect, 6 OUT output, 7 IN passive, and 8 OUT passive; check_footprints resolves Package_SO:SOIC-8_3.9x4.9mm_P1.27mm. These are actual library observations, not manufacturer pinout, enable-polarity, package-correspondence, electrical-suitability, or current-budget verification. The physical SOIC pin map and reported active-low behavior still require exact-device evidence. Connect both OUT pins in the proposed implementation only after that correspondence is verified.

The symbol search found the candidate, symbol_pins returned the complete map above, and the footprint check returned OK. No manufacturer datasheet was independently fetched in this stage. E1/E2 in SPEC.md remain supplied manufacturer-source leads. The tool's passive electrical types on IN and the second OUT pin do not mean those terminals can be omitted or used as ground.

Rationale: installed-library identity makes a candidate drawable; it does not certify the physical part or satisfy the current budget.

### Proposed connections and intentional omissions

Subject to exact-device confirmation: U1.7 IN -> VBUS_RAW; U1.6 and U1.8 OUT -> +5V_PROTECTED; U1.3 GND -> GND; U1.1 EN -> GND; U1.4 ILIM -> ILIM_SET -> R3 -> GND. U1.2 FLG and U1.5 NC remain intentionally unconnected. R3 starts at 301 ohm, 1%.

No FLG pull-up is fitted because status is not read. No VBUS-fed EN bias resistor is fitted because the candidate is always enabled by a direct ground connection. These intentional absences save standing current; confirm that both are legal for the exact -2YM variant before wiring. No MCU is added to control or monitor U1. A passive fuse cannot replace this common active protection.

Rationale: an always-on analog breakout needs neither a programmable controller nor unused status-current paths.

### Load capability, current limiting, and voltage drop

Required normal external load is 500 mA TOTAL, not 500 mA per output and not 500 mA including the indicator. The current-limit lower-bound test is I_LIMIT,min > 500 mA + I_PROTECTED_AUX,max. The latter includes the LED and all downstream leakage or other downstream demand. Considering the LED alone gives a necessary threshold above 500.531 mA; that number is not sufficient if other protected-rail loads exist.

Supplied factors and the initial R3 tolerance give 161/(301*1.01) approximately 0.530 A and 299/(301*0.99) approximately 1.003 A; the supplied typical estimate is approximately 0.764 A. These are conditional calculations, not guaranteed range-wide limits. Verify formula, exact option, voltage/temperature/test scope, resistor temperature behavior, and programming-current definition. Do not select a nominal 500 mA limiter whose low end can prevent the required external load. Conversely, connectors, copper, capacitors, source interaction, and fault testing must account for the credible upper threshold, not just 500 mA normal load.

Supplied 120 milliohm on-resistance at the stated 5 V/500 mA test point gives approximately 60 mV drop and 30 mW dissipation at exactly 500 mA. The real switch carries additional protected-rail demand. These calculations are not guaranteed bounds at 4.75 V, over temperature, or in a short. The output is unregulated and equals input less switch, contact, and copper drops; establish the full loaded-drop bound later without inventing a new regulated-voltage requirement.

Rationale: normal-load delivery, protection spread, source demand, and fault dissipation require different operating cases.

### Fault behavior and reverse power

Supplied research describes MIC2544 current limiting/foldback and thermal cycling rather than latching. Exact-device fault entry, limiting/foldback conditions, thermal behavior, and recovery must be verified. A short on either connector affects the shared rail, the other output, and the LED; there is no independent-channel fault isolation. A sustained short can repeatedly heat/cycle U1. Low normal I-squared-R loss is not evidence of safe indefinite short operation. No physical fault or recovery test has passed.

Outputs are load-only: do not externally energize either output or parallel it with another supply. Reverse-current blocking, reverse-polarity protection, transient immunity, and regulated output voltage are not established capabilities. Any later protective addition must enter both leakage/current and cost accounting.

Rationale: unverified protection capabilities must not be inferred from the presence of a high-side switch.

### Decoupling and startup

C1 and C2 start as 1 microfarad ceramics, rated at least 10 V, packages at least 0603. Supplied input guidance is 0.1-1 microfarad close to U1; exact-device guidance remains to be verified. Check selected dielectric, DC-bias/tolerance/temperature effective capacitance, leakage, and placement. Output bulk capacitance and external load capacitance are not unrestricted: qualify allowable startup demand, charging time, overshoot, and source/protection interaction with the eventual load.

Rationale: nominal capacitor values do not prove decoupling, startup stability, or a current budget. Startup and faults remain separate from settled unloaded operation.

## 4. Parallel external-output subsystem

J2 is a 2-pin, 3.5 mm screw terminal; J3 is a 2x2, 2.54 mm header. Proposed polarity is J2.1 positive and J2.2 GND; J3.1/J3.3 positive and J3.2/J3.4 GND. Positive means +5V_PROTECTED throughout. These assignments are proposals, pending actual symbol pins, footprint pad numbers, and connector drawings. Document the actual viewing orientation and mark pin 1 and polarity on the board.

Either connector alone must deliver the full 500 mA normal external load; both together share that total. Neither the existence of two positive header contacts nor a connector's nominal rating proves that the chosen wiring, contacts, or PCB path carries the specified current. Check exact ratings, mating/terminal-wire access, conductor cross sections, voltage drop, and credible fault exposure during part selection/layout. Keep both paths downstream of U1.

Rationale: parallel outputs provide connection choices, not two independent 500 mA supplies.

## 5. UI and unloaded-current subsystem

The sole UI is an efficient red D1 powered from +5V_PROTECTED through R4, provisionally 10 kohm 1%. It indicates protected-rail availability; it does not prove load capacity, correct USB source entitlement, or absence of faults. Visibility at minimum input and expected viewing conditions remains unverified. Fault collapse or thermal cycling may interrupt the indication.

ASSUMED LED-current calculation uses a 10 kohm 1% resistor with Rmin = 9900 ohm and Vf >= 0 V, giving 5.25/9900 = 0.530304 mA, rounded upward to 0.531 mA. Before treating that allocation as a full-temperature bound, verify that the selected resistor retains R >= 9900 ohm throughout 0-50 degrees C including specified tolerance and temperature effects, or recalculate/reallocate the LED bin and whole-board total. No LED visibility is established by this upper-current calculation.

Rationale: a conservative upper current supports the power budget, but brightness needs actual LED evidence and eventual physical review.

### Complete provisional VBUS-current ledger

Conditions: 4.75-5.25 V, assumed 0-50 degrees C ambient, both external outputs open, U1 enabled and settled, no fault, no backfeed. All values below are allocations in mA, not closed component guarantees.

| Contribution | Ceiling | Present evidence boundary |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| R4/D1 protected-rail indicator | 0.531 | Conservative calculation; selected resistor temperature bound and LED visibility pending |
| U1 internal enabled supply/control | 0.160 | Supplied maximum; test scope and terminal-current inclusion unresolved |
| ILIM/control contribution excluded from preceding figure | 1.000 | Unproven allocation; actual maximum unknown |
| External FLG pull-up/EN bias | 0 | Intentionally absent, conditional on exact-device suitability |
| C1/C2 leakage, combined | 0.050 | Allocation; selected component bounds pending |
| PCB/connector/other fitted protection leakage | 0.050 | Allocation; justified bounds and final inventory pending |
| Other VBUS loads | 0 | None proposed; final fitted inventory must confirm |
| Allocation sum | 1.791 | NOT verified compliance |
| Distance to the exclusive 2 mA boundary | 0.209 | Unallocated planning headroom, not a measured margin |

Trace each physical contribution once. If ILIM/EN current is included in a justified IC supply-current figure, count it there only; if excluded, derive its separate maximum. Do not assume R3 current is below 1 mA because the ledger assigns that amount. Assign input/output capacitor leakage to the correct physical rail while retaining both in the total VBUS budget. CC current supplied by the source on CC is accounted separately and must not be confused with VBUS current.

REQUIRED architecture acceptance gate: do not freeze the active part or RSET until the guaranteed minimum current-limit threshold exceeds 500 mA plus every protected-rail auxiliary/leakage current and the complete, non-overlapping worst-case unloaded VBUS current is strictly below 2 mA over 4.75-5.25 V and 0-50 degrees C with component tolerances. The 1.791 mA allocation is unverified. If the other provisional ceilings 0.531, 0.160, 0.050, and 0.050 mA become justified and remain unchanged, excluded programming/control current must be strictly below 1.209 mA; this conditional residual is not device evidence. Reject or replace a candidate that fails, without relaxing either requirement.

Rationale: this ledger exposes the candidate's unresolved programming-current risk without double counting or converting an allocation into a guarantee. Architecture documentation may proceed conditionally; component acceptance may not.

## 6. MCU, firmware, and connectivity applicability

No MCU, programmable device, onboard firmware, radio, oscillator, memory device, or digital control subsystem is required or permitted by this product architecture. USB-C is a power-input interface only; there is no USB data or PD stack. MCU strapping pins, RTC-capable GPIO, firmware programming interfaces, and RF antenna keepouts are not applicable while this no-MCU/no-radio architecture is maintained.

Retain the original firmware stage. Later confirm the non-applicability conclusion against the selected BOM and actual schematic, and record that stage's genuine result or blocker. Do not create dummy firmware, an unrelated MCU, or fabricated build output to satisfy a file-existence gate.

Rationale: a passive interconnect/indicator with analog active protection needs no software, and truthful applicability is part of pipeline integrity.

## 7. Mechanical, assembly, and cost subsystem

Use at most 40 x 30 mm, two copper layers, 1 oz copper, and nominal 1.6 mm FR-4. The starting rectangular 40 x 30 mm outline has no mounting holes, enclosure, or coating. Assumed use is dry indoor, 0-50 degrees C ambient with ESD-controlled handling. This is not environmental, EMC, ESD-immunity, or regulatory qualification.

Place the eventual USB connector at a board edge according to its drawing, with accessible plug entry, solder row, and shell anchors. Reserve connector access and unambiguous output polarity; keep U1/C1/C2/R3 electrically compact without assigning unverified dimensions or copper widths here. Connector fit, screw access, probe access, usable solder clearances, current-carrying copper, and U1 thermal layout still require actual layout review. No mounting holes are assumed because none are required; revisit if practical handling warrants a documented change.

Use accessible SOIC/leaded IC packages and passives at least 0603. BGA and IC packages with inaccessible underside ground/thermal pads are forbidden. The candidate USB connector's exposed fine-pitch row is an explicit manual-assembly risk. Manufacturer drawings and local footprint availability do not certify hand soldering.

The provisional inventory is J1/J2/J3, U1, R1-R4, C1/C2, and D1. A complete itemized quantity-100 fitted-component BOM must remain strictly below USD 8, excluding PCB fabrication, assembly, shipping, and tax. The supplied 2026-10-08 unit observations are USD 0.83 for U1 and USD 0.5745 for J1, or USD 1.4045 together. This is an incomplete subtotal; every remaining item needs dated evidence or an explicitly uncertain estimate, plus availability/package checks. No complete cost compliance is claimed.

Rationale: the architecture preserves a manually assembled, compact, low-cost target without asserting mechanical fit, actual stock, or a complete BOM before those checks exist.

## 8. Verification interfaces and downstream acceptance

Evidence achieved in this stage: validated documentation proposal; related OpenSpec specs read; installed candidate switch symbol found and actual symbol pins returned; two candidate footprints resolved. These observations do not demonstrate manufacturer pin correspondence, current-budget compliance, fault safety, final cost, or connector fit.

Actual Stage 2 verification: the complete architecture was read back. check_drift returned "no schematic configured; drift vacuously clean". This is a documentation-only result, not a schematic/BOM correspondence check on an implemented circuit. No schematic or board was edited, so ERC, DRC, symbol verification of captured hardware, and schematic legibility were not run; their applicable downstream gates remain mandatory. Rationale: record the observed verification scope without implying hardware checks or physical tests passed.

Before part-selection acceptance, close exact-device pin/polarity and current definitions, guaranteed threshold spread, complete unloaded-current bounds, capacitor suitability, output/contact ratings, LED selection, every part-to-footprint correspondence, and the complete cost inventory. If the active candidate cannot meet both normal-load and unloaded-current requirements, replace it through a documented change rather than weaken the brief. Keep the present candidate conditional until then.

Before schematic completion, inspect actual symbols/pins for every fitted part, preserve the exact architecture identifiers or update them consistently, verify both OUT connections and independent CC nets, and reconcile original symbol checks, ERC, legibility, and drift reports. Board-stage DRC, copper/thermal/mechanical review, and fabrication/render exports remain real downstream obligations. A draft board must identify unrouted connections. This documentation-only stage does not claim an ERC, DRC, or legibility pass for hardware it did not edit.

Physical bring-up remains entirely pending: assembly and polarity; independent CC termination and both plug orientations; known-capable source/cable; settled unloaded current at operating extremes; 500 mA external load on each connector alone and shared; visible LED; loaded voltage drop; startup/inrush; overload and current-limit spread; sustained-short heating/thermal cycling on either output; and recovery after fault removal. Record actual equipment, conditions, results, and uncertainties only when tests run. Check the effects on both outputs and the LED because all share U1.

Rationale: the original eight-stage pipeline and its actual gates remain intact; an architecture draft cannot substitute for downstream artifacts or physical qualification.

# Subsystem architecture: protected USB-C 500 mA breakout

Status: Stage 3 conditional prototype architecture, 2026-10-08. Exact selected MPNs, real pin maps, sources, complete cost/current ledger and UNVERIFIED status are in docs/BOM.md. Native searches/pin lookups and all seven unique footprint resolutions succeeded, except bare passive R/C search queries returned no matches; exact Device:R/C pin lookups proved those symbols exist. No schematic/PCB or physical prototype is produced by this documentation update.

## 1. Topology, identifiers and intentional omissions

J1 VBUS feeds VBUS_RAW and C1, then U1 TPS2065CDBVR feeds +5V_PROTECTED. Both external outputs J2/J3, C2 and the +5V_PROTECTED -> R4 -> LED_A -> D1 anode branch are downstream of U1. D1 cathode and all returns go to GND. Separate R1/R2 connect CC1/CC2 to GND. All J1 VBUS contacts join VBUS_RAW; its four ground contacts plus S1 shield join GND. Data/SBU contacts are intentional no-connects. No USB data, PD, current-advertisement sensing, voltage conversion or reverse-power capability is added.

Current refdes are J1/J2/J3/U1/R1/R2/R4/C1/C2/D1. Nets are VBUS_RAW, +5V_PROTECTED, GND, CC1, CC2 and LED_A. R3 and ILIM_SET are intentionally removed because U1 now has a fixed current limit; do not recycle their identity. EN goes directly to VBUS_RAW and FLT remains unconnected without pull-up. No extra bias resistor, TVS, MCU or unplanned load is fitted. Rationale: retain a single protection domain while eliminating obsolete programming and unused status-current paths.

## 2. Input and USB attachment

J1 is UNVERIFIED USB4105-GF-A with the native Connector:USB_C_Receptacle_USB2.0_16P symbol and resolved exact GCT-model footprint in BOM. Native pins: VBUS A4/A9/B4/B9; GND A1/A12/B1/B12; CC1 A5; CC2 B5; data/SBU A6/A7/A8/B6/B7/B8; shield S1. The source/drawing-overlay distinction and fine-pitch solder risk remain explicit. Supplied ratings are 5 A combined VBUS contacts and 48 V DC, not per-contact 5 A. Direct shield-to-GND is a prototype decision, not an immunity certificate.

Input remains 4.75-5.25 V. R1 and R2 each 5.1k 1% with separate nets support attachment in either orientation. The known-capable source/cable must support 500 mA external load plus board overhead/startup and fault interaction. Rd alone gives no current entitlement. CC-source demand is separate from VBUS-input measurement. Rationale: source contract, attachment, connector rating and the board's measured consumption are different checks.

## 3. Common active protection

UNVERIFIED U1 is TPS2065CDBVR, native Power_Management:TPS2065CDBV, installed Package_TO_SOT_SMD:SOT-23-5. Native pins and supplied TI DBV pinout agree: 1 OUT -> +5V_PROTECTED, 2 GND -> GND, 3 ~FLT -> no-connect, 4 EN -> VBUS_RAW, 5 IN -> VBUS_RAW. Active-high enable and the sole OUT pin replace MIC2544's active-low/dual-OUT topology. No old NC or ILIM terminal exists. Supplied TI DBV drawing has five perimeter leads, no exposed underside pad.

Supplied recommended VIN 4.5-5.5 V covers the original range, 1 A continuous rating covers the normal load, and TJ is -40 to +125 C. Keep actual junction temperature in range; ambient 0-50 C does not itself prove this. With LED 0.540 mA and all 0.100 mA leakage allocations pessimistically downstream, required switched current is 500.640 mA; it fits the 1 A rating and 1.2 A minimum IOS. The maximum static IOS is 1.9 A, so this is not a precise 500 mA cap. Fault copper/contact/source coordination and transient overshoot remain required. Rationale: normal capacity and fault severity are separate constraints.

At 154 milliohm DBV maximum RDS(on), conditional load gives 77.10 mV drop and 38.60 mW conduction loss. Minimum-input switch-only output is approximately 4.67290 V under the stated data conditions; unclosed connector/copper losses further reduce it. No regulated minimum is invented. Normal loss cannot justify indefinite shorts.

Supplied exact-device research establishes active current limiting and disabled-output discharge for this non--2 variant, but does not extract exact thermal/recovery timing. Do not transplant MIC2544 foldback/thermal-cycle claims. Review TI fault/thermal/recovery sections before energized fault tests/release and verify recovery using an energy-limited source. Both outputs and LED are affected by rail collapse; no independent fault isolation or tested short safety is claimed. Output backfeed/paralleled supplies remain prohibited. Rationale: disclose exactly what protection evidence establishes and what it does not.

C1/C2 are each UNVERIFIED 1uF 50 V X7R CC0603KRX7R9BB105, 0603. C1 is close to U1 IN/GND; C2 is protected-rail bypass. Supplied TI input recommendation is >=0.1uF; nominal 1uF gives useful margin but guaranteed effective capacitance including DC bias/temperature/aging is unverified. Validate startup and external capacitance, overshoot and source interaction. Rationale: a nominal value is not a transient or effective-capacitance guarantee.

## 4. Parallel outputs

UNVERIFIED J2 is Phoenix 1984617: 3.50 mm, 2-pin screw terminal, pad 1 positive and 2 GND. UNVERIFIED J3 is Harwin M20-9980246: 2x2 2.54 mm header, pads 1/3 positive and 2/4 GND. Native connector symbols have the exact real pins documented in BOM. Supplied unrotated footprint geometry is J2 pads (0,0)/(3.5,0); J3 pads 1=(0,0), 2=(2.54,0), 3=(0,2.54), 4=(2.54,2.54) mm. State the actual component-side orientation and mark polarity after final placement; unkeyed mating cannot enforce it.

Either connector alone must carry 500 mA external load; together they share 500 mA total. Supplied nominal ratings are J2 17.5 A and J3 3 A/contact. Never rely on equal sharing of header contacts. Keep every positive branch downstream of U1. J3 finished-hole interval must be 0.97-1.07 mm although installed nominal drill is 1.00 mm; confirm fabrication tolerances. Support J2 housing against screw torque. Rationale: pin identity, connector rating, fabricated geometry and actual loaded paths require separate verification.

## 5. Indicator and complete conditional VBUS current ledger

UNVERIFIED D1 WP710A10LID uses native Device:LED (1 K to GND, 2 A to LED_A) and the resolved 3 mm THT footprint. R4 is 10k 1% RC0603FR-0710KL. Supplied 2 mA optical data does not prove visibility near the approximate 0.33 mA operating point. Test minimum-input visibility and rerun the budget if R4 changes. Resistor tolerance plus 100 ppm/C over 0-50 C gives a modelled Rmin 9875.25 ohm and maximum 0.531633 mA at 5.25 V with Vf>=0; revise the old 0.531 mA allocation to 0.540 mA, retaining aging/process qualification.

Unloaded VBUS allocations in mA: LED 0.540; U1 IN bias 0.190 (0.090 supplied maximum at IOUT=0 plus 0.100 unverified reserve for the LED-loaded condition); separate EN terminal 0.001; absent external pull-ups 0; C1/C2 leakage 0.050; PCB/connectors 0.050; other VBUS loads 0. C1/C2 supplied IR supports only its stated 15-35 C test point. FLT has no external VBUS current path without a pull-up, and no RSET exists. Count IN/EN/LED/capacitor/board paths once, never add a second copy of a current already included in a later total measurement. CC Rd current is separate from VBUS.

Explicit sequencing decision: replace the Stage 2 model-added pre-BOM guaranteed-closure gate with conditional UNVERIFIED prototype selection. Before release/qualification, still demonstrate strict <2 mA over 4.75-5.25 V and assumed 0-50 C with all tolerance/temperature effects and full 500 mA external delivery. Known violations still require rejection/redesign. Record the change, not a silent exception. All original software gates remain. Rationale: the requested artifact is a reviewable prototype; conditional budgets can inform capture without making a false compliance claim.

## 6. Mechanical, assembly and cost

Retain <=40 x 30 mm, two 1 oz copper layers, nominal 1.6 mm FR-4; assumed rectangular 40 x 30 mm with no holes, enclosure or coating, dry indoor 0-50 C and ESD-controlled handling. No environmental/EMC/ESD qualification exists. The ten-refdes inventory is conditionally suitable for accessible manual prototype assembly: SOT-23 perimeter leads, >=0603 passives and THT outputs/LED. Exact package/source correspondence and unresolved conditions are in BOM, including USB/U1 drawing overlay, header finished-hole control and LED manufacturer's repair/rework-only manual-solder guidance. No unqualified manufacturer endorsement is asserted.

Future layout must check every courtyard, board-edge/plug/solder access, screwdriver and wire entry, LED lead stand-off, header mating/strain relief, copper drop/current and fault thermal area. No actual fit or assembly test is reported. Rationale: source-backed geometry supports drafting; the fabricated result remains to be verified.

Complete estimated component cost is USD 2.5439/board at Q100, including an explicitly uncertain J2 estimate of USD 0.590 from a Q1-only observation. Other line prices are dated Q100 snapshots; R1/R2 and C1/C2 each require 200 pieces at 100 boards but use the known 100+ tier without invented discounts. The strict <USD 8 target is unchanged. Header Q100 procurement is unresolved because the source showed only 5 stock and 22-week lead time. No purchase, delivered quote or guaranteed availability is claimed. Rationale: count every fitted part while disclosing uncertainty rather than refusing to estimate permitted costs.

## 7. MCU, firmware and downstream verification

The actual selected BOM contains no programmable device, MCU, radio, firmware, oscillator or digital interface. Firmware remains not applicable at BOM level; retain the original firmware stage and report its genuine result/blocker after confirming against the later schematic. Do not create dummy code or bypass any original eight-stage gate. MCU strapping, RTC GPIO and antenna checks are inapplicable while none of those devices exists.

This stage is documentation/selection only. Its actual library results do not constitute schematic ERC, symbol-implementation, legibility, board DRC or drift checks against captured hardware. Run and read actual check_drift before completion; do not infer its result here. Later schematic and PCB gates, fabrication/render exports and draft/unrouted labels remain mandatory.

All physical bring-up remains pending: assembly/polarity; CC separation and both orientations; capable source/cable; whole-range settled unloaded current; 500 mA on either output and shared; LED visibility; full loaded drop; startup/capacitance/inrush; exact fault/recovery data review; current-limit spread/overshoot; sustained-short heating and thermal behavior; recovery after fault removal; effects on both outputs and LED. No measurement or qualification has been performed. Rationale: preserving evidence boundaries is part of completing a truthful prototype pipeline.

References: docs/SPEC.md for current constraints; docs/BOM.md for exact sources and per-refdes details; docs/DECISIONS.md for the recorded replacement, omissions and gate revision. Historical Stage 2 MIC2544 choices remain in the changelog/decision history only.
